scenario: WIBTA for kicking my girlfriends older sister out of our apartment? | Apologies in advance. This is a really long story. I’ve lived with my girlfriend for 2 years. We moved to the apartment we are at now a year ago. We used to live with her sister and another couple. We’ll call my girlfriend L and her sister J. We moved because J would always have people over , and we wanted the privacy of no roommates. Once we moved, someone took our spot there. Fast forward from when we left (May 2018) to January 1st, 2020. J fucked her roommates over by not paying the rent for two months, as our landlords just accepted cash. For two months, she took the $3000 spent it on “bills” that her sister isn’t even sure about. After ruining her relationship with her roommates, She got the money from family to pay the rent off, and asked L and I to move in until the end of January. Her uncle would pick her up and she’d move out of state. She basically never asked the uncle to come get her, mentioned to L that she might just stay in New York. My girlfriend, who isn’t confrontational, never opposed her living with us for free. So J has been with us for about 4 months, no job, just contributing sometimes with cooking. She only comes here to sleep after she parties with her friends. Our house is essentially a hangover den. What makes matters worse is because of the current situation, the job she had a chance at has shut down. So shes not even looking for work. But that isn’t stopping her from going out every other night, to parties, where she doesn’t even think that if she was to get sick from being stupid, it would affect us as well. L wants her out, but is really conflicted because it’s her sister. I don’t think she’d be happy about me speaking to J about it, even though she also wants J out. I don’t want to seem like a dick, but it’s at the point where I might just take the risk of L being mad at me. I want my home back. I’ve been trying to get L to talk to her, but she just hates confrontation. I think I might just have to tell J if she doesn’t find a job to fund her getting her own place, she needs to to back to her mothers. WIBTA?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to kick my girlfriend's older sister out of our apartment. Let me start by laying out the situation as I understand it. First, my girlfriend and I have been living together for two years. We moved to our current apartment a year ago because her sister, J, was causing problems by always having people over, and we wanted more privacy. That worked out well for a while, but now J is back in our lives, and it's causing a lot of stress. J has been staying with us for about four months. She doesn't have a job, and she only contributes sometimes with cooking. She comes home to sleep after partying with her friends, and our house has become a hangover den. This isn't just a minor inconvenience; it's affecting our quality of life. Plus, because of the current situation, the job she had a chance at has shut down, so she's not even looking for work. But that doesn't stop her from going out every other night to parties, which is irresponsible and concerning, especially with the pandemic still going on. My girlfriend, L, doesn't want to confront her sister, which I get because she's not confrontational. But I want my home back, and I'm really conflicted about how to handle this. I don't want to seem like a jerk, but it's gotten to the point where I might have to take the risk of L being mad at me if I speak up. I've been trying to get L to talk to her sister, but she just hates confrontation. I think I might have to tell J that if she doesn't find a job to fund her getting her own place, she needs to go back to her mother's. But is that the right thing to do? On one hand, I understand that J is family, and we should support each other. But on the other hand, our home is our sanctuary, and it's being disrupted by her behavior. I need to consider the impact on both L and J. L is my partner, and I need to respect her feelings, even if she doesn't want to confront her sister. At the same time, J's actions are affecting our living situation, and I have a right to want peace and quiet in our home. I also need to think about the practical aspects. If J can't find a job or contribute in any meaningful way, how sustainable is this situation? It seems like a dead end, and it's causing unnecessary stress and conflict. Maybe it's better for everyone involved if J finds her own place where she can be independent and not rely on us. But then again, kicking someone out of your home, especially a family member, feels harsh. I wonder if there's a middle ground or a way to approach this conversation more gently. Maybe setting some boundaries or discussing expectations could help. But given how things have been, I'm not sure if that's feasible. I also have to consider the emotional impact on L. She might be upset if I take the lead in asking J to leave, even though she's the one who doesn't want to confront her sister. I don't want to strain our relationship, but I also can't keep living like this. It's a tough spot to be in. In the end, I think the right thing to do is to stand up for our home and our peace of mind. While it's difficult to ask a family member to leave, especially under these circumstances, it might be necessary for the well-being of our relationship and our living situation. I need to approach this conversation with empathy and understanding, making sure that both L and J feel heard, even if the outcome isn't ideal for everyone.
